title: Add RAG agent templates, tool-calling examples, and docs site updates
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: provide first-class RAG/agent templates and concrete tool-calling quickstarts for developers to onboard faster and to demonstrate Redwood's structured output + tool-calling ergonomics. This PR adds opinionated RAG templates, multiple agent examples (Python/TS), and updates the docs site quickstarts with runnable snippets, test fixtures, and a small e2e example that exercises tool-calling flow. Checklist: - [x] Add RAG templates (retriever + prompt scaffolding) - [x] Add Python and TypeScript agent examples demonstrating tool-calling and function-like responses - [x] Update redwood-docs quickstarts and guides with runnable snippets and copy - [x] Add link-check and lint exemptions for external example links - [x] Add unit tests and simple CI job for examples Usage notes: - Examples live in redwood-examples/rag-agent-templates and redwood-examples/agents/tool-calling. The quickstarts document under redwood-docs now includes step-by-step instructions to bootstrap a RAG agent using Redwood SDKs, configure a retriever, and wire in a local tool (example: simple calculator HTTP tool). - Tool-calling examples show structured response handling and graceful fallback to text-only responses if the tool is unreachable. - The templates include recommended KV cache and batching settings for common RAG workloads. Related: ENG-3124 (RAG quickstart), ENG-3167 (tool-calling patterns). Testing: added unit tests for example snippets and a lightweight e2e that runs the TS example against a local mock tool. CI notes: initial run hit a transient docs link-check failure (external example CDN); link-check re-run passed. Merge plan: squash-merge after approvals. Release notes: documented new quickstarts and example locations in the docs site and examples repo.
